To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

BSA adsorption on negatively charged silica surfaces is dominated by long-range electrostatic interactions and that these electrostatic interactions are responsible for orienting the BSA on the surface.

(a) the long-range electrostatic forces between the BSA protein and the silica surface are attractive, and are the dominant force driving adsorption, (b) the short-range forces between the BBA protein and the silica surfaces are repulsive and prevent adsorption, and (c) the orientation of the BSA protein on the silica surface is dictated by a competition between the long- and short-range interactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the adsorption of a negatively charged protein to a negatively charged oxide surface, and the consequences that this has on the structure and orientation of the adsorbing protein.
the fundamental interactions between proteins and surfaces, and provides insight into how the adsorbed protein structure impacts their functionality.
the fundamental interactions that govern the adsorption of proteins to inorganic material interfaces.
